meta.title: BMW Engine Rebuild & Repair Specialists | Boby Engine Work
meta.description: BMW engine rebuilding, reconditioning and repair at Boby Engine Work. Coverage across diesel, petrol and M engines with written scope before work begins.

paragraphs: BMW engine failure rarely announces itself gently. A diesel 320d can lose timing; a six-cylinder petrol can show low oil pressure; an M-car can develop a knock that stops being background noise. What the badge says and what is fitted can differ, so the right first step is identification, not a guess.

paragraphs.text: At Boby Engine Work, we specialise in BMW engine rebuilding, reconditioning and repair. From a 320d with timing damage to a six-cylinder petrol BMW with oil consumption or pressure concerns, we assess the engine already in the car and quote to the findings — not a generic menu price.

paragraphs: With more than 10 years of workshop experience and 1,000+ clients across the business, we focus on German and premium vehicles where correct parts, measurement and assembly matter.

section2.intro: Our BMW coverage includes major combustion-engine models from the last three decades, together with selected older cars. Model names organise the enquiry; exact engine and generation checks determine the work.

paragraphs: We cover the 1 Series, 2 Series, 3 Series, 4 Series, 5 Series, 6 Series, 7 Series and 8 Series. This includes relevant saloon, Touring, coupé, convertible, Gran Coupé and Gran Turismo versions, as well as Active Tourer and Gran Tourer applications within the 2 Series range.
The smaller cars can require the same careful engine work as a larger executive BMW once the correct engine identity is confirmed.
Our model coverage includes X1, X2, X3, X4, X5, X6 and X7, with the installation checked for the relevant sDrive or xDrive version.
The Z Series route covers Z3 and Z4 enquiries where the fitted engine and service history need to be confirmed before quoting.
We assess 1M Coupé, M2, M3, M4, M5, M6, M8, X3 M, X4 M, X5 M, X6 M and XM engine work.
M Performance versions such as M140i, M240i and M340i sit with their respective model families; they are not automatically the same engine as a full M car and are quoted individually.

A BMW badge does not tell us which engine is fitted or how it failed. A 320d may carry an N47, B47 or another diesel four-cylinder depending on year and market; a petrol six-cylinder enquiry may be N-series or B-series; an M-car needs its exact S-engine confirmed.
approach.quote: We start with registration, symptoms and history, then match what we find to the appropriate inspection route — timing, lubrication, cooling, turbocharging and contamination are checked in context, not from a one-size label.
approach.closing: Alongside BMW we service Mercedes-Benz, Audi, Volkswagen, Porsche, MINI, Jaguar and Land Rover; enquiries for those brands follow the same assessment-first approach.

items.title: Diesel: M47, M57, N47, N57, B47 and B57
items.text: The generation and installation determine how we inspect timing, lubrication, bearings, cooling and contamination. If there is an oil-pressure warning or deep knock, stop the engine and describe when it first appeared.

items.title: Petrol: older engines, N-series and B-series
items.text: BMW petrol enquiries span older four- and six-cylinder units, N20/N54/N55 turbo engines and B38/B48/B58 applications. Smoke or oil use can come from ventilation, turbocharger sealing or internal wear; testing identifies the likely route before major work is authorised.

items.title: M and performance engines
items.text: S54, S55, S58 and other performance engines call for individual scope and parts decisions. An M Performance badge does not make the car mechanically identical to an M3. We quote to the actual engine and installation.

blocks.title: Repair or Rebuild the Engine Already in Your Car
blocks.text: Where the core is suitable, rebuilding the fitted engine keeps the original installation matched to the vehicle. Scope depends on inspection — heads, blocks, timing, lubrication and ancillaries are assessed before major parts are ordered.

blocks.title: Replacement-Engine Enquiries Begin with an Assessment
blocks.text: A replacement route is discussed when rebuild is not appropriate or not economic. We still need the same vehicle details, symptoms and history; supplier engines are not quoted sight-unseen.

steps.title: Enquiry and Vehicle Identification
steps.text: We record model, registration, mileage, symptoms and any prior work so the correct engine family is in view before the car arrives.

steps.title: Arrival and Initial Diagnosis
steps.text: Fault codes, oil condition, cooling history and running checks are matched to the symptoms described at enquiry.

steps.title: Engine Removal Where Required
steps.text: Access and workshop handling are planned; some preliminary checks may be possible in the bay before removal.

steps.title: Strip-down and Inspection
steps.text: Components are cleaned and examined for wear, cracking, contamination or impact damage.

steps.title: Measurement and Machining Decisions
steps.text: Heads, blocks and rotating assemblies are measured; machining is agreed only where the specification requires it.

steps.title: Parts Selection and Assembly
steps.text: Approved components are fitted with checked clearances and correct torques for the specific BMW engine.

steps.title: Initial Running and Checks
steps.text: Oil pressure, leaks and relevant diagnostics are monitored on first start.

steps.title: Road Testing Where Appropriate
steps.text: Drive cycles confirm temperatures, performance and noise under load when safe to do so.

steps.title: Collection and Aftercare
steps.text: You receive an explanation of work completed, running-in guidance and warranty terms.

items.title: Warranty
items.text: Rebuilds and replacement engine work carry a 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty on the engine scope agreed in writing, subject to terms. Ancillaries such as turbochargers are excluded unless itemised.

items.title: Running-In Service
items.text: A running-in service is required at Boby's workshop, typically around 2,000 miles after collection, so fluids and fasteners can be checked under load.

items.question: Does a BMW timing-chain fault always need an engine rebuild?
items.answer: No. Some timing-related faults have a smaller repair scope if caught early and inspection shows contained damage. If timing has been lost, mechanical consequences must be checked before a limited repair can be recommended.

items.question: Do you rebuild older BMW engines?
items.answer: Yes. Enquiries cover older combustion-engine BMWs and later models; exact generation and engine code still need confirming before quoting.

items.question: Can I get a price without knowing the engine code?
items.answer: You can start with registration, model, year and symptoms. We identify the likely engine, then confirm what is fitted before a written quote is issued.

items.question: Do you sell brand-new BMW engines?
items.answer: The focus is repair and rebuild of the engine you have. Replacement supply is discussed only when appropriate after assessment.

items.question: How long will the rebuild take?
items.answer: It depends on diagnosis, machining and parts lead time once the engine is inspected. We discuss timing after the initial assessment.

items.question: Can you help if the BMW no longer starts?
items.answer: Yes. Describe whether the car rolls, where it is and any recent work. Collection across mainland UK can be quoted separately where needed.
